subject: ApertureAI performance — executive status & mitigation digest
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aperture.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cindy Lopez <cindy.lopez@aperture.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Abrupt latency + 5xx spike on prod (region-us-west)

Vanessa —

We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and a rise in 5xx error rate across our production traffic to the Redwood hosted endpoint (region: us-west). Impact started ~07:40 PT and is still ongoing. Throughput is capped intermittently; some requests queue up then error.

I attached a short telemetry dump (aperture-slo-telemetry-20270502.csv). Key customer impact: search autocomplete and chat assistants show 10–30s response times and a 7% 5xx rate. This is affecting our live rollout.

Please advise urgently — we need a coordinated plan and executive point of contact.

— Sanjay
Head of Engineering, Aperture AI
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aperture.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, Cindy Lopez <cindy.lopez@aperture.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Abrupt latency + 5xx spike on prod (region-us-west)

Sanjay — thanks for the telemetry and the clear summary. We're pulling an urgent cross-functional bridge. I've attached a one-page mutual action plan (redwood-mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf) and proposed timeline.

Immediate steps (ETA and owners):
- 09:15 PT: infra triage (Marissa) — surface pod/queue saturation, kernel traces.
- 09:30 PT: runtime & model config check (Karthik) — verify batching/quantization swaps and kernel selection.
- 09:45 PT: routing & rate controls (Aditya) — apply temporary rate cap and route to fallback model variant if needed.
- 10:00 PT: exec sync (me + Laura) — provide CEO-level summary and escalation runbook.

We propose a brief exec touchpoint at 10:30 PT (15 min) to confirm responsibilities and public-facing comms. Can you confirm availability for a 10:30 standup and whether we should include your Head of Product?

We will avoid any disruptive model reloads unless explicitly coordinated.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success 
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aperture.ai>, Cindy Lopez <cindy.lopez@aperture.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Abrupt latency + 5xx spike on prod (region-us-west) — triage notes

Team — quick triage findings from the initial sweep (logs + node metrics):
- Root symptoms: queue growth on us-west inference pool, GPU utilization ~95% on several nodes, and preemption events coincident with a scheduled batch policy change at 07:30 PT.
- Error signature: grpc 14 (connection/transport) and HTTP 504s originating at the routing layer when KV cache misses cascaded into longer decode paths.
- Correlation: a recent client-side burst (higher batch sizes from Aperture traffic ~07:36) increased tail latency.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:10–09:25):
- Increased max worker threads on affected pods (Marissa).
- Reverted aggressive local batching override for the affected customer namespace (Karthik).
- Applied a soft rate cap at the gateway for Aperture requests (Aditya) set to 80% of recent peak to allow backpressure to drain.

Next actions (owners):
- Log-level RCA & kernel trace analysis (Marissa) — deliver first findings by 12:00 PT.
- Telemetry capture of request paths + kv-cache hit ratios (Karthik) — push a second dump to the shared link.
- Customer communication draft for external stakeholders (Vanessa + Laura) — share public note by 10:45 PT.

I've attached interim telemetry and flagged INC-1987 in Jira.

— Marissa
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aperture.ai>, Cindy Lopez <cindy.lopez@aperture.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-02T10:41:00-07:00
Subject: ApertureAI — 10:30 exec touchpoint notes & committed runbook

All — notes from the 10:30 exec sync and commitments for the ApertureAI leadership team. Thank you for joining. This message is the single source update for external stakeholders.

Executive summary (what happened):
- A late-night client-side burst combined with a recently tightened batching override created queue pressure → KV cache misses amplified decode latency → routing layer hit timeouts (result: 5xx and higher p99 latencies).

Customer impact: autocomplete and assistant features experienced 10–30s tail latency and ~7% 5xx over a 45-minute window.

Actions we committed to (short horizon, visible to customer):
1) Traffic management: keep soft gateway rate cap (80% of peak) until stable — owner: Aditya (complete).
2) Fallback routing: serve a validated lower-latency model variant (reduced batch sensitivity) for Aperture namespace for next 3 hours — owner: Karthik (deployed at 10:15 PT).
3) Infrastructure: add two additional workers in us-west pool and increase pod concurrency where safe — owner: Marissa (in progress).
4) Monitoring & RCA: 12:00 PT delivery of first findings; full RCA within 72 hours — owner: Marissa + Karthik.
5) Customer comms & credits: proposed goodwill credit to cover impacted tokens; draft sent to Aperture procurement (Cindy) for review — owner: Vanessa + Laura.

Public-facing customer note (short):
- "Aperture AI — We identified increased request queuing that caused elevated tail latency and errors. We've applied a temporary traffic cap and routed traffic to a lower-latency model variant while we stabilize the pool. Expect improved response times within the hour. Our team will share a formal RCA within 72 hours and a proposed credit schedule."

Attachments: redwood-mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf, fallback-model-config-brief.txt
Jira: INC-1987

We will keep this channel updated. Sanjay/Cindy — please reply here with observed improvements and any business-critical checkpoints (e.g., live demos, rollback windows).

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aperture.ai>, Cindy Lopez <cindy.lopez@aperture.ai>, procurement@aperture.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: ApertureAI — 24-hour status & remediation progress

Sanjay / Aperture team —

24-hour status update following yesterday's incident:
- Stabilization: throughput and tail latency have returned to baseline for the past 16 hours; current p99 is within agreed SLOs and 5xx is <0.5%.
- Permanent mitigations in progress: a new batching guardrail will be added to the customer namespace to prevent client-driven oversizing; we're also scheduling an auto-scaling window refinement for the us-west pool to reduce cold-start/throttle coupling.
- RCA timeline: preliminary RCA (with kernel trace highlights and the exact sequence of events) will be delivered by 2027-05-05 17:00 PT. Full RCA + remediation plan with target commit dates is due by 2027-05-06.

Customer offer: to acknowledge operational impact, Redwood proposes a token credit for the impacted window and a one-time free consulting session to tune Aperture's batching configuration. We will route the formal credit proposal to procurement after your sign-off.

Next steps (actionable):
- Please confirm that you see restored performance in your region:us-west telemetry (Sanjay).
- If you require an independent post-incident call with our CTO + your engineering leadership, we can schedule one within 48 hours.

Appreciate your patience — we will send the preliminary RCA as promised.

— Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aperture.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Cindy Lopez <cindy@aperture.ai>, procurement@aperture.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ApertureAI — 24-hour status & remediation progress

Vanessa / Laura / team —

Thanks — we confirm the production p99 and error rates are back to normal and our customers are no longer seeing degraded responses. The temporary routing to the fallback model visibly reduced tail latency within ~20 minutes of deployment.

We'd like the preliminary RCA as soon as it's ready and please include: exact config deltas, timestamps of the batching override change, and the reasoning for why the routing timeouts did not trigger automatic fallback earlier. Also confirm the timeline for the proposed credit and the consult.

Appreciate the responsiveness and the clear runbook — looking forward to the RCA.

— Sanjay
Head of Engineering, Aperture AI
